title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 62 (Further Issue of Share Capital)

content.overview: Section 62 governs further issue of share capital. Where a company with a share capital proposes to increase subscribed capital by issue of further shares, such shares must be offered to existing equity shareholders in proportion to their paid-up share capital (rights issue), subject to the right to renounce. Alternative routes include issue to employees under ESOP or to any persons (preferential basis) if authorised by special resolution, on conditions prescribed. Time limits and notice requirements apply to the rights offer.
content.glance: Further shares: first offer to existing equity holders pro rata (rights issue with renunciation); or ESOP; or preferential issue on special resolution and prescribed conditions.
content.study: Where at any time a company having a share capital proposes to increase its subscribed capital by the issue of further shares, such shares shall be offered to persons who, at the date of the offer, are holders of equity shares of the company in proportion, as nearly as circumstances admit, to the paid-up share capital on those shares by sending a letter of offer subject to prescribed conditions; the offer must state the number of shares offered and limit the time (not less than fifteen days and not exceeding thirty days) within which the offer if not accepted will be deemed declined; unless the articles otherwise provide, the offer includes a right of renunciation. Notwithstanding the rights route, further shares may be offered to employees under a scheme of employees’ stock option subject to special resolution, or to any persons (whether or not including existing shareholders or employees) if authorised by special resolution, either for cash or for consideration other than cash, subject to prescribed conditions including valuation. Current-law framing: identify proposed further issue; apply rights offer as default; or map ESOP/preferential special-resolution routes and conditions.

sections.heading: Rights Issue (Default)
sections.body: Further shares offered to existing equity holders in proportion to paid-up capital; letter of offer with 15–30 day window; renunciation unless articles exclude.

sections.heading: ESOP Route
sections.body: Offer to employees under ESOP scheme with special resolution and prescribed conditions.

sections.heading: Preferential Issue
sections.body: Offer to any persons on special resolution, for cash or non-cash consideration, subject to prescribed conditions including valuation.

examples.title: Rights offer
examples.body: The company sends a letter of offer to equity holders pro rata, with a 21-day acceptance window and renunciation right. Section 62 rights route is followed.

examples.title: Preferential issue
examples.body: By special resolution and with prescribed valuation, the company issues further shares to a strategic investor. Section 62 preferential route is used.

hypotheticals.question: Can the company issue further shares only to outsiders without a special resolution?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The default is a rights offer to existing equity holders. Preferential issue to others requires a special resolution and prescribed conditions under s. 62.

distinctions.title: Further issue (s. 62) vs private placement (s. 42)
distinctions.left: Rights / ESOP / preferential further issue framework
distinctions.right: Private placement of securities to identified persons

misconceptions.trap: Board can always issue further shares to anyone without shareholder approval.
misconceptions.correction: Default is rights issue to existing equity holders; ESOP and preferential routes need special resolution (and prescribed conditions).

enhancement.definition: Section 62 requires further shares to be offered first to existing equity holders pro rata (rights issue), with alternative ESOP and preferential routes on special resolution and prescribed conditions.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Existing equity holders have a statutory pre-emptive opportunity unless a special-resolution alternative route is validly used.
